subject: pair-implementer
reason: Ownership check via caller identity (404), 409 problem for non-cancellable orders with a narrow catch, and the request row recorded only on success so failed cancels commit nothing; all callers updated, build and 43 tests pass. New members (CancelOrderResult, BuyerIdentityGuid, the new Handle) have no prior callers.

follow_ups.title: IdentifiedCommandHandler swallows all exceptions and commits the idempotency row for failed commands
follow_ups.reason: Create, ship and the order status commands still return default on any exception while the transaction commits the request row, so a retry of a failed request is treated as a duplicate.

items.reason: Two concurrent requests with the same x-requestid can both pass ExistAsync and cancel the order; the second CreateRequestForCommandAsync then throws and the request returns 500 (the race already existed).
items.fix: Optional follow-up: treat a duplicate-key failure on the request row as a duplicate request.

items.reason: The CancelOrderCommand case in the generic IdentifiedCommandHandler is now unreachable because the cancel handler no longer derives from it.
items.fix: Optional: remove the dead case, or leave it as is.

subject: pair-implementer
reason: Buttons per status, the successful cancel and the in-flight disabled button all work in the browser, but when the ordering API is unreachable the cancel post returns a bare 500 error page because the list load in OnInitializedAsync is not guarded. The 409 path could only be checked in code because this stack's API does not return 409.

items.reason: With the ordering API stopped, clicking Cancel order makes POST /user/orders return 500 and the page shows only 'Error: 500 Internal Server Error'. On the form post, OnInitializedAsync calls OrderingService.GetOrders() with no try/catch, and its HttpRequestException escapes before CancelOrderAsync can catch it. A timeout fails the same way.
items.fix: Catch HttpRequestException and TaskCanceledException around the GetOrders call in OnInitializedAsync and show the message, or skip the initial load on the cancel post since CancelOrderAsync reloads the list anyway.

items.reason: The cancel PUT goes through the standard resilience retry. When the API answered 500 for an order that was already Paid, the PUT was retried with the same x-requestid and the duplicate request came back 200, so the page showed no message and the order stayed Paid. A 409 is not retried, so this goes away once the API answers 409, but any other 500 on cancel is still hidden.
items.fix: Consider turning off retries for this non-idempotent PUT, or file it as a follow-up for the API's request-id handling.

items.reason: At 375 px, rows with a Cancel order button wrap differently from the other rows: the status drops below and the date and total columns no longer line up.
items.fix: Give the actions cell its own full-width line on small screens so the other columns keep their positions.

items.reason: A .visually-hidden class is defined again in the page's scoped CSS instead of reusing a shared style.
items.fix: Reuse an existing shared utility or put it in app.css.

subject: pair-implementer
reason: All acceptance criteria hold in the running app: Cancel order appears only on Submitted/AwaitingValidation/StockConfirmed rows, a cancel issues one PUT and the row reloads as Cancelled, and API failures show an alert instead of an error page; the 409 path is correct in code but could not be exercised live because this slot runs the base Ordering API. Only minor UX/cosmetic notes remain.

items.reason: Because the page uses [StreamRendering] and OnInitializedAsync returns early on a cancel post, the first streamed chunk of the POST replaces the whole list with 'Loading your orders...' while the cancel runs; the button is removed rather than shown disabled/busy (a double submit is still impossible: one PUT observed).
items.fix: Optionally keep the list visible during the cancel post (e.g. load orders before the handler or skip the loading branch when a cancel is in flight) so the disabled/busy button stays on screen.

items.reason: The existing '.orders > p' rule is more specific than '.orders-message', so the alert text uses --color-ink-2 / --text-lg instead of the intended danger colour and base size.
At 375px, rows with a Cancel order button wrap unevenly (date centred, total pushed right, status and button on a second line) while other rows keep their single-line layout.
items.fix: Optionally let the actions cell take its own full-width line at phone width so the other columns keep their usual alignment.
